newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich will not seek leadership if Democrats win.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich will not seek leadership if Democrats win.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich has said he would not seek another leadership role in Congress if Republicans lose control of the House of Representatives. But he also has no plans to resign from office, a Gingrich aide said Monday.
With only two weeks to go before the Nov. 5 election, the prospect of Republican losses in House races across the country is fanning speculation about Gingrich's political future.

John Ellis, former President George Bush's nephew who writes a conservative political column for the Boston Globe, said Gingrich recently informed top fund-raisers at a breakfast meeting that he would resign rather than face a House ethics investigation in the hands of Democrats.
The claim appeared in the Boston Globe on Saturday, bringing vehement denials from the Gingrich camp.

"It's a total fabrication. Newt never said that. Newt does not intend on resigning his seat under any circumstances," said Mike Shields, a spokesman for the Gingrich re-election campaign in Georgia's 6th Congressional District.

"And to say such a thing would have anything to do with the ethics investigation is utterly ridiculous, because he's had 74 of the 75 charges dropped. He's been found innocent more often than anyone else in politics."

After the Ellis column appeared, Gingrich took the unusual step of issuing a statement denying "the ridiculous assertion" and underscoring his belief that the Republican House majority would grow in November, not disappear.

"What I actually said was that if the Democrats gain control of Congress, I would not seek a leadership position. This is because the Democrats, as a majority, would take a hard turn to the left," the 53-year-old former House minority whip said in the statement.
"The job of the Republican leadership in a minority would be reduced to simply opposing (Democrats), to be negative."
Ellis, who described himself as a Gingrich supporter, said he regretted any trouble he caused for the speaker but stuck to his story.
Ellis claimed Gingrich had threatened to resign as speaker on a number of occasions, as a ploy to squeeze money out of Republican contributors.
"The person who gave me a rundown on what happened said he wasn't sure if Gingrich was trying to get them to raise more dough," said Ellis.
"I don't know that he had any real intention of stepping down as speaker at that point, and I have no real knowledge of whether he intends to step down as a congressman," he continued.
"It's possible there was a misunderstanding. If there was, I regret it. But I don't think there was."
